feature_issues.body:
Part of https://github.com/llvm-mos/llvm-mos/issues/32 . This issue is a (simpler) specialization of the problem space presented in https://github.com/llvm-mos/llvm-mos/issues/319 , but still requires a lot of consideration with regards on how to implement it.

Note that this issue alone, without implementing 16-bit register modes, allows for the development of 65816 targets; the only remaining distinction for 65816 "native mode" is adjusting llvm-mos-sdk's crt0 to initialize the stack pointer to $01FF rather than $FF on such targets.
feature_issues.title: [65816] 24-bit address space support

feature_issues.body:
Part of https://github.com/llvm-mos/llvm-mos/issues/32 .

The main challenge here is being clever about emitting REP/SEP instructions to switch, and deciding which register widths to support and how - while the 8-bit registers A and B are effectively subsets of their 16-bit counterpart, they are not as cheap to access as on most LLVM-supported architectures; in addition, the 8-bit registers X and Y cannot be treated as subsets of their 16-bit counterparts, as their high portions are reset when the 16-bit index register mode is disabled.

Note that a target which provides the 65816's 16-bit register modes, but not the 24-bit address space, is already present in llvm-mos-sdk as "rpc8e" (RedPower 2's RPC8/e "fantasy" computer), and may as such prove useful for testing.
feature_issues.title: [65816] 16-bit register mode support

inspection: Read-only source, test inventory, two legalizer test files, and ten most recent commits affecting MOSLegalizerInfo.cpp at the pinned destination. No destination compiler build or independent review.
finding: The destination legalizer admits 8- and 16-bit pointers and narrows ordinary scalar loads to 8 bits. Its addressing-mode selector has no 32-bit pointer branch. The inspected source lacks tryFarRuntimeIndexFold, getFarOffsetMax, and the Accum16/Index16 feature queries. Existing 65816 instruction support does not supply this native far-word pipeline.
preparation: 0070 is a downstream delta on the native/far feature stack including 0062, the runtime far-index fold, and 0069. Extract and validate with the compiler/ABI series for issues #320/#321.
publication: Local draft only. Evidence links require published immutable commit URLs before posting.
scope_note: This is an optimization preparation record, not a new compiler defect or a change to existing defect status.
